name: norvel
author: music-rhythm-and-dance agent
description:
norvel v6 (direction: music, rhythm and dance) - A DRUM GRID: THE SNARE HIT WITH NO HAT
OVER IT SKIDS LATE. PRIVATE; never shown to players. Earlier versions: norvel.v1..v5.json.

WHY v6. v5 is calibrated ON RATE (6 Opus finals of the identical v4 design: 100/100/100 % with a
demo, 15/14/14 % without) but the judge scores the kid test 3.67 twice running. The v5 verdict:
"the remaining friction is the three-row, multi-bar column bookkeeping itself - matching
hat-column to snare-column to kick-column by eye; try a visual anchor that lets the eye find
'hat hole above a snare hit' without manual column counting". v6 is that anchor, taken to its
conclusion: ONE comparison instead of two (the kick row is gone) and the hat's holes are drawn
"_" instead of ".", so "a gap over a hit" is a single local shape and nothing has to be counted
along a row. The rule loses one conjunct and the picture loses a third of its glyphs; the rate
profile (the ~12 % foothold, the unguessable rendering) is kept and re-measured.

CLUE = A FINISHED DRUM GRID, three lines (seed 77):

      hat |x_xx|xx_x|_xxx|_x_x|x__x|
    snare |.x..|x...|x...|.x..|.x..|
    3 snare slip

SOLUTION = the same picture with the snare row edited:

      hat |x_xx|xx_x|_xxx|_x_x|x__x|
    snare |.-x.|x...|-x..|.x..|.--x|
    3 snare slip

THE RULE (one clause). A snare hit with NO HAT ABOVE IT - a hit sitting under a gap in the hat's
ticking - skids late: it is drawn "-" where it stood, "-" on across the gap, and lands "x" on the
first step where the hat is ticking again. Nothing else changes. Kid sentence from one demo:
"if the hat isn't ticking over a snare hit there's nothing holding it, so it slides along until
the hat comes back in." In the demo above the hit in bar 1 and the hit in bar 3 each skid one
step; the hit in bar 5 sits under a two-step gap and skids two, landing where the hat returns;
the hit in bar 2 has the hat above it and stays; the hit in bar 4 stays too - the gap is next to
it, not above it. Four kinds of near-miss, one demo, one row to look at.

THE THREE DRAWINGS THAT WERE MEASURED (3000 fresh clues each, same rule throughout)
  A  TWO ROWS, gaps drawn "_"  (SHIPPED)   39.8 glyph cells, 1 row to compare, longest line 37,
     every skid's origin and landing separate marks in 68 % of demos (83 % per skid).
  B  THREE ROWS, gaps drawn "_" (v5 + the anchor only)  59.7 cells, 2 rows to compare, longest
     line 37, readable demos 35 %. Every row re-run against it comes back v5's to the second
     decimal (echo 12.80 %, "ghost + one step later" 21.40 %, and v5's "lone hits but only when
     no kick lands on the landing step" 18.83 % for BOTH v5 and B): the anchor costs nothing and
     buys nothing but the glyph - the kick column still has to be matched by eye, in the other
     direction, which is what the judge objected to.
  C  ONE ROW OF TWO-CHARACTER BEATS ("beat x. _x x. x. | xx x. _. x. | ..."), hat over snare
     inside each cell. The pairing becomes a token (`_x`) and needs no eye-tracking at all, but
     the line is 72 characters (against 37), there are no rows left, and the drum tab stops
     looking like a drum tab: this is the "opaque code" that DESIGN_LOOP says scores 2/5 on
     clue_shape. Rejected on the object, not on the rate.
A also beats B on the number that decides the blind rate: the best rendering a demo-less player
can guess falls from 21.4 % to 17.7 % (the n = 1 skid is two steps half the time now). The best
wrong rule in the v6 rival set is 20.9 %; the two rivals the single comparison invites are
planted to 0.00 % (change 3). The wrong-rule columns of A and B are not directly comparable -
a two-row rule and a three-row rule have different rivals - so B is quoted from v5's own table.

WHAT CHANGED IN v6
1. THE KICK ROW IS GONE. v4/v5 asked for "no hat above it AND no kick under it": two columns to
   match, in opposite directions, before the question even opens. v6 asks one question about the
   row directly above. The selection becomes visible in the picture, and that is deliberate -
   the caption's offline checksum is now nearly free, but the checksum was never the difficulty
   (tovel3a's notes, lad-tovel-v7-3: "norvel | count certain, edit unknown | UNKNOWN (11 edits
   tried)"). What the demo sells is the RENDERING, and no rendering is guessable from the clue:
   the best blind attack still scores 17.70 %.
2. THE HAT'S HOLES ARE DRAWN "_". A gap in the ticking now looks like a gap. "_" over "x" is one
   local shape; the eye finds it without counting steps, and in the answer the dash trail lies
   exactly under the "_" run, so the demo shows the hit crossing the gap and landing where the
   hat comes back. The scorer maps "_" to "." before comparing, so an answer that redraws the
   gaps as dots (or keeps them) scores identically (measured 100 % on 3000 clues).
3. TWO NEW PLANTS, BOTH ABOUT "ABOVE". Every clue carries a gap RIGHT AFTER a snare hit and a gap
   RIGHT BEFORE one, with those hits staying put. They are the near-miss the single comparison
   needs - the gap has to be over the hit, not beside it - and they take the two rivals that this
   simplification invites from 18.9 % and 34.0 % to 0.00 %.
4. THE n = 1 SKID IS TWO STEPS HALF THE TIME (v5: never). "It moves one step later" is now
   contradicted by the harvest as well as by every n >= 2 picture, and the best blind rendering
   drops 21.4 % -> 17.7 %.
5. ONE HIT THAT STAYS HAS MORE ROOM AFTER IT (>= 3 free steps) THAN ANY HIT THAT SKIDS. v5's
   readable-landing preference had leaked into "the n hits with the biggest gap after them"
   (20.3 %); with this decorrelation the preference can be kept at full strength and that rival
   sits at 18.5 % while readable demos go 35 % -> 68 %.
6. The grid is v5's, B = (4,4,5,5,6)[n] - 4.97 bars - but two rows instead of three: 39.8 glyph
   cells against 59.7, longest clue line 37 chars, clue <= 88 chars against 126. Smaller was
   tried and rejected: at four bars the n = 2 and n = 3 clue spaces collapse to 27 % and 2 %
   distinct pictures over 60 000 seeds (against 97 % and 83 % at five bars), and a harvest of
   ~30 DIFFERENT clues is what the caption's offline work needs.
7. The caption is unchanged - "<n> snare slip", the verb and the count - and the house rule holds:
   the answer may keep it, drop it, reword it, move it or use v4's old "n slip" (all 100 %).
   REJECTED AGAIN, with reasons: "hi-hat" as a label ("-" is a compared glyph, so a dash in a
   label corrupts its row); a fancier bar line (solve/score walk the grid by skipping "|");
   drawing the snare with drum-tab "o" (it would put "o" in the compared alphabet, and a prose
   line like "moved two" then becomes a spurious row - the len > 3 line filter now covers that
   case, but the leniency is not worth the risk).

CONSTRUCTION (generate). B = (4,4,5,5,6)[n]; m = B..B+3 snare hits (>= n+2), never two adjacent
and never on the last step; the hat plays every step except the gaps, at most 2 per bar. n is
drawn 0(12 %)/1(10 %)/2(29 %)/3(29 %)/4(20 %) BEFORE any retry, so the distribution is exact.
Every clue plants the near-misses that make one demo enough:
  * >= 2 snare hits with the hat still ticking above them          (they stay)
  * >= 1 gap RIGHT AFTER a hit and >= 1 gap RIGHT BEFORE a hit     (those hits stay)
  * >= 2 gaps over empty steps, one of them with nothing beside it in 54 % of clues (nothing
    happens under an empty gap)
  * n >= 2: one skid of one step and one of two steps in the same picture; n = 1: two steps half
    the time
  * one hit that stays has >= 3 free steps after it, more than any skidding hit
and n is refused whenever it equals a count a player could read straight off the picture (snare
hits, bars, gaps, gaps that are not over a hit, hits that stay) so the caption cannot be
explained by anything but the rule. All 3000 sampled clues carry every plant; 1 fallback in
60 000 seeds; 92 % of 60 000 clues are distinct pictures (86/95/97/83/98 % for n = 0..4).

INTENDED DISCOVERY PATH. (a) from the clue alone: a drum part, hat over snare, the answer is this
picture with the snare row edited - the caption says which row and how many - so a demo-less
player echoes the clue and banks the ~12 % of clues that say "0 snare slip"; (b) the selection is
visible: the hits standing under a gap in the hat, and the caption confirms it on the first
harvested clue instead of the thirtieth; (c) the demo is the only place the EDIT appears - a dash
where the hit stood, dashes across the gap, the hit landing on the first tick after it; (d) both
skid lengths live in the same picture, so "until the hat comes back" is forced rather than "one
step later".

WITNESS TABLE (3000 fresh clues)
  the true rule (solve)                                                     100.00 %
  clue echoed unchanged (the foothold: the "0 snare slip" clues)             12.80 %
  RIGHT HITS, WRONG DRAWING (a player without the demo):
    hit moves one step later, no ghost                                       12.80 %
    ghost + hit one step later                                               17.70 %
    ghost at the origin only, lands right                                    17.70 %
    hit stays + a copy one step later / glyph change in place                12.80 %
    moves to the landing without ghosts / stays + a copy at the landing      12.80 %
    ghosts but skidding EARLIER / landing on the previous tick               12.80 %
    the hit is simply deleted / dashes over the gap but the hit stays        12.80 %
    lands on the last step of the gap                                        12.80 %
    skids one step too far                                                   15.37 %
  RIGHT DRAWING, WRONG HITS (a player with the demo):
    every snare hit skids                                                     0.00 %
    lone hits + the hits just AFTER a gap / just BEFORE a gap                  0.00 %
    every hit just before a gap (not under one)                               0.00 %
    the same edit applied to the hat row                                      0.00 %
    every hit with >= 2 free steps after it                                   0.03 %
    all the lone hits but the last                                           12.80 %
    the n leftmost snare hits                                                14.30 %
    only the hits under a TWO-step gap / only under a ONE-step gap     16.50 / 17.70 %
    the n hits with the biggest gap after them                               18.53 %
    the n rightmost snare hits                                               20.90 %
  demo replay / empty / junk / unicode / 4000 chars / snare row alone / rows swapped /
    the snare row shifted one step / all on one line / one wrong hat cell /
    a third (kick) row added                                                  0.00 %
  leniency (all 100 %): bare rows with no bars and no labels, other labels, a "|1234|" beat
    header, blank lines, CRLF, tabs, prose around the picture (with or without full stops),
    spaces around the bar lines, the gaps redrawn as dots, the caption kept / dropped /
    reworded / moved / replaced by v4's "n slip"
Gradient: 0 % (well-formed but the wrong hits) -> 12.8 % (the format and the "0" clues) ->
15-21 % (the right hits with the drawing wrong, or a plausible wrong selection) -> 100 %.
Nothing without the insight exceeds 21 %.

VALIDATION. quickcheck --seeds 200: OK, one warning ("score accepts the clue itself as a
solution") which is the intended n = 0 foothold and is raised identically by kelmar, fennick and
durnel. score 317/512, solve 372/5000, generate 4438/50000; clue <= 88 chars (v5: 126),
solution <= 88. generate deterministic, 0.26 ms mean over 60 000 seeds (worst 3.9 ms, 1 fallback
in 60 000); solve 0.002 ms and scores 1 on 3000/3000 fresh clues; score 0.016 ms (0.065 ms on
junk). Scorer: 0 raises, 0 non-binary results and 0 false positives on 12 000 junk strings; 0
disagreements with an independent re-implementation on 24 000 mutated answers.

LEVERS. Too easy (a demo-less player cracks the rendering): drop the ghost dashes across the gap
so the drawing is one "-" and one "x"; make the gap over a skidding hit sometimes three steps
wide; stop printing the caption on 1 clue in 4. Too hard (a demo-holder stays under 30 %): let
the skid always be one step; guarantee two skidding hits in the same bar; put a worked skid into
the clue.
generate:
# THE PICTURE: two drum rows over B bars of four steps -- the hat on top, drawn "x"
# where it ticks and "_" where it stops, and the snare under it -- plus a caption
# "<n> snare slip".  THE RULE (one clause): a snare hit with NO HAT ABOVE IT -- a hit
# sitting under a gap in the hat's ticking -- skids late: it is drawn "-" where it
# stood, "-" on across the gap, and lands "x" on the first step where the hat is
# ticking again.  n counts the skidding hits and is 0 in ~12 % of clues, where the
# echoed clue scores.  The gap glyph is the visual anchor: "a hole above a hit" is one
# local shape, so nothing has to be counted along a row to find it.
# B = (4,4,5,5,6)[n] is the smallest grid that still carries every plant, and every
# clue plants the near-misses that make ONE demo enough:
#   * >= 2 snare hits with the hat still ticking above them        (they stay)
#   * >= 1 gap RIGHT AFTER a hit and >= 1 gap RIGHT BEFORE a hit   (those hits stay:
#     the gap has to be ABOVE the hit, not next to it)
#   * >= 2 gaps over empty steps, often one with nothing beside it (nothing happens)
#   * when n >= 2, ONE skid of two steps and ONE of a single step, so no constant
#     distance renders the answer and the demo shows the hat catching the hit
#   * one hit that STAYS has more room after it than any hit that skids, so "the hits
#     with the most space after them" cannot reproduce the caption
FB = ("  hat |_xxx|xxxx|xx_x|x_xx|\n"
      "snare |.x..|.x.x|....|x.x.|\n"
      "0 snare slip")


def generate(seed):
    r = random.Random(seed)
    n = 0 if r.random() < 0.12 else r.choice((1, 2, 2, 2, 3, 3, 3, 4, 4))
    for _ in range(500):
        B = (4, 4, 5, 5, 6)[n]                       # the smallest grid that fits
        L = 4 * B
        m = r.randint(max(B, n + 2), B + 3)          # snare hits, never adjacent
        S = sorted(r.sample(range(L - m), m))
        S = [p + i for i, p in enumerate(S)]         # gaps >= 2, last step free
        Ss = set(S)
        cand = list(S)
        r.shuffle(cand)
        cnt = [0] * B                                # hat gaps per bar: at most 2
        A = []
        for w in (1, 0):                             # the hits that skid: prefer a
            for a in cand:                           # landing that reads clearly
                if len(A) < n and not cnt[a // 4] and (
                        not w or (a + 2 not in Ss and a + 3 not in Ss
                                  and all(abs(a - b) > 4 for b in A))):
                    A.append(a)
                    cnt[a // 4] = 1
        if len(A) < n:
            continue
        # a two-step skid: the hat is missing over the next step as well.  Always one
        # when n >= 2, half the time when n == 1, so neither a single clue nor a
        # harvest of them supports "it just moves one step later".
        el = [a for a in A if a + 2 < L and a + 2 not in Ss and cnt[(a + 1) // 4] < 2]
        want2 = (n > 1) or (n == 1 and r.random() < .5)
        if want2 and not el:
            continue
        ext = set()
        if want2:
            ext.add(el[0] + 1)
            cnt[(el[0] + 1) // 4] += 1
        keep = {a + 1 for a in A} | {a + 2 for a in A}   # the hat must come back here
        holes = set(A) | ext
        free = [i for i in range(L) if i not in Ss and i not in keep and i not in ext]
        r.shuffle(free)

        def add(pool):                               # one more gap over an empty step
            for i in pool:
                if i not in holes and cnt[i // 4] < 2:
                    holes.add(i)
                    cnt[i // 4] += 1
                    return 1
            return 0

        got = add([i for i in free if i + 1 in Ss and i + 1 not in A])
        got += add([i for i in free if i - 1 in Ss and i - 1 not in A])
        if got < 2:                                  # a gap just after and just before
            continue                                 # a hit that stays put
        if r.random() < .5:                          # a gap in the middle of nowhere
            add([i for i in free if i + 1 not in Ss and i - 1 not in Ss])
        if n:                                        # a hit that stays has the most
            gp = {}                                  # room after it of anything here
            for k, i in enumerate(S):
                gp[i] = (S[k + 1] if k + 1 < m else L) - i - 1
            if not [i for i in S if i not in A and gp[i] >= 3]:
                continue
        # counts a player could read off the picture instead of finding the rule
        if n and n in (m, B, len(holes), len(holes) - n, m - n):
            continue
        row = lambda f: "|" + "|".join(
            "".join(f(4 * b + j) for j in range(4)) for b in range(B)) + "|"
        return ("  hat " + row(lambda i: "_" if i in holes else "x") + "\n"
                + "snare " + row(lambda i: "x" if i in Ss else ".") + "\n"
                + str(n) + " snare slip")
    return FB
solve:
def solve(clue):
    H, S, T = clue.split("\n")
    E = list(S)
    for i, q in enumerate(S):
        if q == "x" and H[i] == "_":          # a hit with no hat ticking above it
            j = i
            E[i] = "-"
            while H[j] == "_":                # skid on across the hat's gap
                j += 1 + (S[j + 1] == "|")
                E[j] = "-"
            E[j] = "x"                        # land where the hat ticks again
    return H + "\n" + "".join(E) + "\n" + T
